entry.title: The One-Way Door — Purpose Charter Academy's Access Denial Pattern
entry.content:
Two Staff. Two Incidents. One Policy.

Incident 1 — August 29, 2026 (Physical)

A parent with legal custody arrived at Purpose Charter Academy, 10101 East Canfield, Detroit.

Giselle — the receptionist — denied the parent access to their child.

Brian Roderick Banks — the school’s operator — told Detroit Police officers he is “an attorney.” He is not an attorney. The State Bar of Michigan returns zero results for “Brian Banks.” He has 9 criminal convictions (6 felony), including assault with intent to murder.

The police escorted the parent off school property based on Banks’ false representation.

DPD Report #26-0909-0176. The report exists. The badge numbers exist. The custody order exists.

Incident 2 — October 12, 2026 (Phone)

A caller dialed (313) 767-3100 — Purpose Charter Academy’s main line.

Ms. Perkins — the receptionist — answered.

The caller asked about Banks and DaSean.

Ms. Perkins stated:

  • She has not seen Banks today
  • She has not seen DaSean today
  • She has not seen anybody

School is in session. She is at the reception desk. She answered the phone. She is not blind.

She lied.

The caller has called before. This is not the first contact.

The Pattern

DateStaffMethodWhat they saidTruth
Aug 29GiselleIn person[Banks]: “I am an attorney”He has never been admitted to any bar. 9 convictions.
Oct 12Ms. PerkinsPhone“Haven’t seen Banks, haven’t seen DaSean, haven’t seen anybody”School in session. She’s at the desk. She answered the phone.

Two staff members. 44 days apart. Same conduct: deny that anyone is present, deny access to the child.

This is not two individuals making personal choices. This is institutional policy. Someone trained them. Someone told them what to say.

The One-Way Door

Purpose Charter Academy is a one-way door:

What goes INWhat stays OUT
Public education dollars ($4.9M/yr)Parents with custody rights
Children (enrolled by parents who trust the school)Information about those children
72.67% of revenue → The Purpose Group LLCAccountability
Board members (a judge, an AAG, a council member)Oversight

The receptionist is the membrane. She is the operational layer between a parent and their child. On August 29, Giselle was that membrane. On October 12, Ms. Perkins is.

The name at the desk changes. The policy doesn’t.

The Perkins Question

Ms. Perkins at the PCA reception desk shares a surname with three people already documented in the network:

NameRoleConnection
Todd PerkinsBanks’ personal attorneyPerkins Law Group, Detroit. Represented Judge Miller in DTW gun case.
Judge Sean Perkins36th District CourtTodd’s brother. Worked at Todd’s firm before the bench.
Judge David Perkins3rd Circuit CourtFamily donated to Banks-aligned campaigns.

Three Perkins in the legal/judicial layer protecting Banks. One Perkins at the school reception desk denying access to a parent.

Is Ms. Perkins related to Todd and Sean Perkins?

We don’t know yet. The surname match is documented. The question is asked. The answer will come from the sweep.

What the Law Says

FERPA (20 U.S.C. §1232g): Custodial parents have the right to access their children’s education records and information about their children at school.

MCL 380.1137: Schools shall not deny a parent access to their child except by court order.

MCL 600.916: It is illegal to represent yourself as an attorney if you are not one. Banks did this on August 29 to justify denying access. DPD Report #26-0909-0176 documents it.

A receptionist saying “I haven’t seen anybody” is not a legal basis for denying a parent information about their child. It is a lie designed to end the conversation.

Ask for Brian Banks. Ask about your child. Listen to what they tell you.

Then read this page again.

entry.title: The Dykema Chronology — 1988 to Present
entry.content:
How to Read This

Every entry has a date, a source, and the actors/entities involved. The timeline traces one law firm’s connections across 36 years — from shelf corporations in 1988 to charter school board governance in 2026.

This is not a conspiracy theory. It is a public record.

Phase 1: Building the Legal Framework (1982–1997)

1982 — McLellan Joins Dykema

Richard D. McLellan’s private practice merges with Dykema Gossett. He becomes head of the Government Policy & Practice Group and Managing Member of the Lansing office. He had previously served on Gov. William Milliken’s staff.

Source: Wikipedia; McLellan biography, Mackinac Center.

Actor: Richard McLellan (Dykema partner, Lansing)

1987 — McLellan Co-Founds Mackinac Center

McLellan co-founds the Mackinac Center for Public Policy, a free-market think tank that will become the intellectual engine behind Michigan’s charter school movement. He serves as board secretary for decades.

Source: Mackinac Center

Actors: Richard McLellan, Joseph Olson

1988 — Dykema Registers Shelf Nonprofits

Dykema registers pre-formed nonprofit entities — empty corporate shells ready for activation:

Dykema Gossett Nonprofit Shelf Corporation800865335Aug 16, 1988Dissolved
Dykema Gossett Shelf Nonprofit Club Corporation800797761Oct 7, 1988Dissolved

Filed by Cindy M. Wilder at 800 Michigan National Tower, Lansing (Dykema’s former Lansing office). Dissolved within months.

Source: Michigan LARA Business Entity Search

Entity: Dykema Gossett PLLC

1990 — McLellan Runs Engler Transition

McLellan serves as transition director for Governor-elect John Engler. This positions Dykema at the center of the incoming administration that will create charter schools.

Source: Wikipedia; Mackinac Center biography

Actors: Richard McLellan, John Engler

Oct 5, 1993 — Engler Proposes Charter Schools

Governor Engler proposes charter school legislation in a speech before a joint session of the Michigan Legislature.

Source: Founders Library

Actor: John Engler

Dec 3, 1993 — Dykema Writes the Charter School Law

SB 896, creating Part 6a of the Revised School Code, passes the Legislature. Richard McLellan and Leonard Wolfe of Dykema Gossett are the “leading legal architects” of the legislation.

McLellan personally conducted “12 hours of shuttle diplomacy” in the Senate Majority Leader’s conference room to negotiate a version that would survive constitutional challenge.

The law allows:

  • State universities, community colleges, ISDs, and school districts to authorize charter schools
  • For-profit management companies to operate charter schools
  • A 3% authorization fee (incentivizing authorizers to keep schools open)
  • No statutory authorizer evaluation system
  • Board members appointed without identity disclosure requirements

Source: Founders Library; MI Good Government; Dykema.com Education page

Actors: Richard McLellan, Leonard Wolfe (Dykema)

Jan 14, 1994 — Engler Signs PA 362

Governor Engler signs the charter school law. Michigan becomes the 9th state to enact a charter school law.

Source: Founders Library

Actors: John Engler, Richard McLellan, Leonard Wolfe

1994 — First Charter Schools Open

Central Michigan University becomes the first authorizer. Three schools open: Casa Maria Academy (Detroit), New Branches School (Grand Rapids), Northlane Math and Science Academy.

Source: CMU Center for Charter Schools

1997 — Dykema Defends the Law at Supreme Court

The Michigan Education Association challenges the constitutionality of PA 362. Dykema’s McLellan and Wolfe defend the law before the Michigan Supreme Court in Council of Organizations and Affiliates v. Engler, 455 Mich 557 (1997).

The Court upholds the law and orders state funding restored.

Court record lists: “Dykema, Gossett, P.L.L.C. by Richard D. McLellan, Lori M. Silsbury, and Leonard C. Wolfe, Lansing, for intervening Defendants-Appellants.”

Source: Justia; 455 Mich 557

Actors: Richard McLellan, Leonard Wolfe, Lori Silsbury (Dykema)

Phase 2: The Machine Operator Arrives (2009–2016)

W. Alan Wilk begins his entity formation practice. First documented entity:

EntityLARA IDYear

Wilk serves as legal and compliance officer for Governor Snyder’s NERD Fund (New Energy to Reinvent and Diversify). The fund:

  • Raised $2.19M from undisclosed donors over 3 years
  • Paid Rich Baird’s $100K salary
  • Paid EM Kevyn Orr’s travel expenses
  • Shut down in 2013 after transparency criticism

Source: Detroit News, Nov 19, 2014

Actors: W. Alan Wilk (Dykema), Rick Snyder, Rich Baird, Kevyn Orr

2011 — Wolfe Lifts the Charter Cap

Leonard Wolfe “plays instrumental role” in SB 618 (signed Dec 20, 2011), which phases out the cap on university-authorized charter schools. Wolfe attends the signing ceremony with Governor Snyder.

This removes the 150-school limit that had constrained charter expansion since 1999.

Source: Dykema.com

Actors: Leonard Wolfe (Dykema), Rick Snyder

2012 — Banks Elected to State House; Wells-Stallworth Joins MacDowell Board

Brian Roderick Banks elected to the Michigan House of Representatives (D-Detroit). Serves as Chair of the Detroit Caucus.

Nicole Wells Stallworth appointed to MacDowell Preparatory Academy board. She will serve continuously for 14 years.

Source: purposecharteracademy.com; charterschools.org

Banks and Ellison were MSU Law classmates (2010).

Source: PACER, W.D. Michigan

Source: Free Press, Aug 27, 2023

Wilk incorporates Our Neighborhoods First (LARA 802493189). Officers include Keenann Knox (Impact Church), Lorna Thomas (Public Lighting Authority chair, Duggan appointee), Betty Brooks (ex-police commissioner, “dear friend” of Duggan for 30 years).

Renae Moore serves as both Dykema employee AND compliance officer for the Duggan campaign AND recordkeeper for ONF.

Source: Deadline Detroit

Actors: W. Alan Wilk, Keenann Knox, Renae Moore, Lorna Thomas, Betty Brooks

Aug 10, 2021 — Detroit Leaders Assumed Name

SDJ registers assumed name “Detroit Leaders” — one week after Latisha Johnson and Steve Elrick advance to the general election in District 4. Detroit Leaders sends mailers supporting Johnson against Elrick.

Source: Deadline Detroit

Actors: Latisha Johnson, Steve Elrick, Keenann Knox, W. Alan Wilk

Aug 25, 2021 — FBI Raids Carol Banks

FBI raids Carol Banks’ East English Village home as part of “Operation Northern Hook” — the public corruption investigation that produced Councilman Andre Spivey’s bribery conviction. Agents seek records on 501(c)(4) organizations and campaign financing.

Source: Free Press, Aug 25, 2021

Nov 2021 — Johnson Wins, Elrick Loses

Latisha Johnson defeats journalist Steve Elrick in Detroit District 4. The dark money entity formed by Dykema’s Wilk helped defeat the journalist who covered Banks’s network.

Source: Wayne County election results

Actors: Latisha Johnson, Steve Elrick

Phase 4: The Board Is Captured (2022–2025)

Aug 2022 — Banks Applies for School Administrator Certificate

Ten days after losing his county commissioner race, Banks applies for a school administrator certificate from MDE. Granted the next day (Sep 2, 2022 — school starts Aug 29).

Source: Free Press, Aug 27, 2023; MDE records

Actor: Brian Banks

Feb 2022 — MDE Investigates Banks’s Credentials

MDE sends letter to Wells-Stallworth (MacDowell Board Chair) warning that Banks’s employment “may be in violation of the State School Aid Act.” Banks has no valid Michigan teaching credential.

MDE gives the school a procedural loophole rather than enforcing compliance.

Source: MDE FOIA response, Sep 25, 2026

Actors: Brian Banks, Nicole Wells Stallworth, MDE

Jun 2023 — Wells-Stallworth Defends Charter Board Governance

Wells-Stallworth publishes Bridge Michigan op-ed: “Michigan charter school boards ensure financial accountability.” She presides over a board approving 72.67% revenue extraction to Banks’s management LLC.

Appears on MAPSA podcast: “A Charter School Board Member Tells All.”

Source: Bridge Michigan, Jun 9, 2023

Jun 2023 — Wilk Forms Put Progress First

Wilk incorporates Put Progress First — a nonprofit backing Duggan’s leadership, signaling a possible gubernatorial bid. Same Dykema formation pattern.

Source: Bridge Detroit

Aug 2023 — Free Press “Back to Fool”

Michigan legislature passes charter reform requiring authorizers to review contracts over $100K, attend 50%+ of board meetings, and mandate audited EMO financials. This legislation is directly responsive to governance failures like Banks’s operation.

Fair Use Notice

This page is a public-interest commentary and analysis of “It Had 2 Happen: The Agony of Success” (ISBN 173575403X, True Vine Publishing Co., 2020) by Brian Banks, J.D. All excerpts are used under the fair use doctrine, 17 U.S.C. § 107, for purposes of criticism, commentary, and public interest reporting.

Four-factor fair use analysis:

  1. Purpose: Non-commercial criticism, commentary, and public-interest journalism. This site has no advertisements, no donations, no monetization. The purpose is to protect 362 children attending schools operated by the book’s author.
  2. Nature of the work: A published autobiography — the lowest tier of copyright protection. Self-published, commercially available, and branded with credentials the author does not hold.
  3. Amount used: Selected excerpts only, each accompanied by original commentary and cross-referenced against independently verifiable public records. No chapter is reproduced in full.
  4. Market effect: None. Amazon ranked this book #2,637,193 in Kindle Store (per M.L. Elrick, Detroit Free Press, 2022). This commentary does not substitute for the original work.

The book’s own copyright page states: “a reviewer may quote brief passages in a review.” This is a review.

The book is also a party admission under Michigan Rule of Evidence 801(d)(2)(A) — Banks’s own published statement, offered against him as a named party in pending litigation (Mok v. Banks et al., Case No. 2026-4349-CZ, Ingham County Circuit Court). Every word is admissible. No foundation required beyond authentication. The ISBN authenticates it.

Banks has no copyright claim that survives fair use. An attempt to suppress this analysis would constitute a SLAPP action against protected criticism of a public figure (former State Representative) regarding matters of profound public concern (credential fraud affecting public schools).

The Book

The author is credited as “Brian Banks, J.D.” on the cover, copyright page, and all retail listings. The State Bar of Michigan returns zero results for “Brian Banks.” He was denied bar admission on Character & Fitness due to nine criminal convictions. The J.D. degree is real. The right to use it as a professional credential is not. 📄 Documented

The Credential Fraud Begins on the Cover

Banks’s biography page — the final section of the book — reads:

“Honorable Brian R. Banks, M.Ed., J.D.”

Three false credential claims in six words:

  1. “Honorable” is a title reserved for judges and elected officials. Banks resigned from the legislature in 2017 after his ninth conviction. He is not a sitting official.
  2. “J.D.” implies a licensed legal practitioner. Banks has never been admitted to any bar.
  3. The biography states he aspired to “become a prominent attorney and, then, sit on the bench as an officer of the court” — admitting the exact goal he has been fraudulently representing as achieved.

The biography further claims:

“He has earned a Juris Doctor with a Concentration in Criminal Law from Michigan State University College of Law”

True. He earned the degree. He was never licensed to practice.

“Mr. Banks is a highly sought-after consultant, educator, organizer, assistant, community, political, legal mind and now, an author.”

“Legal mind.” Not “attorney.” Not “licensed.” The phrasing is a carefully constructed near-claim — close enough that readers assume licensure, vague enough to defend as technically truthful. This is how credential fraud works when the person committing it went to law school.

entry.title: The Credential Gap — MacDowell Staff Qualification Audit
entry.content:
The Michigan Online Educator Certification System (MOECS) is the public database where anyone can verify whether a Michigan educator holds a valid teaching certificate, administrator certification, or permit — and which grade levels and subjects each endorsement covers. 📄 Documented

On September 26, 2026, every name listed on MacDowell Preparatory Academy’s public staff roster (macdowellprep.com/about/) was searched in MOECS. The audit found that only 2 of 14 instructional staff members are properly credentialed and correctly placed for their teaching assignment. 📄 Documented

Staff Roster Results 📄 Documented

Administration — 4 positions ($603,000/year combined)

RoleMOECS StatusIndicator
Superintendent/CAO (Brian Banks)Convicted felon (ICHAT SID 2029469K). School Administrator certificate only — no teaching credential.❌
Dean of Scholars + Culture (Cameron Coleman)Standard teaching certificate expired 6/30/2026. No administrator certification for Dean role.⏳
Dean of Academics (Kellie M Stevens)Standard teaching certificate (K-5/K-8 elementary). No administrator certification for Dean role.⚠️
Dean of Operations + 8th Grade Teacher (Chalcee Norwood)Not found in MOECS public search — 91 “Norwood” results searched, no match for “Chalcee”. Zero credentials discoverable.❌

Instructional Staff

RoleMOECS StatusIndicator
Kindergarten (Rachel Webb)Holds Secondary English/Journalism 6-12 certification. Zero elementary endorsement. Teaching kindergarten with a high school certificate.⚠️
Kindergarten (Lakeisha Bates)“No matches found” in MOECS. Zero credentials.❌
3rd Grade (Alana Hubbell)Daily Substitute Permit issued through Escuela Avancemos — a different school.🔶
5th Grade (Ashlie Spencer)Daily Substitute Permit issued through Chandler Park Academy — a different school.🔶
8th Grade Teacher (Volanda Frazier)Full-Year Basic Substitute permit only — no standard teaching certificate. Assigned as full-time Teacher of Record.⚠️
2 instructional staffProperly credentialed and correctly placed for their assignment.✅
2 staffExpired or pending credentials.⏳

Legend: ✅ Valid · ⚠️ Wrong endorsement/placement · ❌ No credentials · 🔶 Substitute permit from other school · ⏳ Expired

Source: MOECS public credential search, September 26, 2026. Staff titles from macdowellprep.com/about/.

The Rachel Webb Finding 📄 Documented

A kindergarten teacher holds a Secondary English/Journalism certification endorsed for grades 6–12.

Elementary education in Michigan requires a specific endorsement in early childhood or elementary education. A 6–12 secondary certification does not qualify an educator for K–5 instruction under Michigan law. MOECS shows Rachel Webb’s only endorsements are English 6–12 and Journalism 6–12 — neither covers kindergarten.

The Substitute Permit Problem 📄 Documented

Two MacDowell instructional staff hold Daily Substitute Permits issued through different schools:

StaffAssignmentPermit Issued Through
Alana Hubbell3rd GradeEscuela Avancemos — Detroit
Ashlie Spencer5th GradeChandler Park Academy — Harper Woods

Daily Substitute Permits are tied to the issuing school and are intended for temporary fill-in duty, not permanent full-time instructional positions. Using substitute permits from other schools to staff ongoing teaching roles is a credential compliance issue under Michigan law.

Volanda Frazier holds a Full-Year Basic Substitute permit as the full-time 8th grade Teacher of Record — a separate but related compliance problem.

The Law — MCL 388.1763 📄 Documented

Michigan Compiled Laws require charter school teachers to hold valid credentials:

“A teacher employed by or assigned to a public school academy shall hold a valid Michigan teaching certificate or a permit issued by the superintendent of public instruction.”

Penalty provisions when violations are found:

StatuteRequirement
MCL 388.1763(1)A district shall not employ an individual who is not appropriately placed under a valid certificate.
MCL 388.1763(2)50% state aid deduction for salary paid during the violation period.
MCL 388.1763(6)If a school official is notified by MDE and knowingly continues to employ an uncredentialed individual → misdemeanor, $1,500 fine per incident.

When MDE identifies credential violations, the statute requires enforcement — state aid deductions for uncredentialed employment and, where officials continue employment after notification, referral for criminal prosecution.

What MDE Did 📄 Documented

MDE was notified of credential problems at MacDowell. Over a four-year period, the Office of Educator Excellence investigated only one name — Brian Banks — in February 2022. The investigation was closed within approximately two hours after OEE Analyst Katie Schmiedeknecht communicated that “there will be no need for an investigation.”

MDE never checked the rest of the staff roster — despite MOECS and the Educator Registry (REP) being MDE’s own systems, searchable by any analyst in minutes.

Schmiedeknecht presents at state conferences on the same credential compliance rules she is charged with enforcing — including slides stating that “Any teacher who is not appropriately placed may be subject to a salary deduction based on MCL 388.1763.” Her office failed to enforce those rules at MacDowell while advising the school through the compliance loophole that avoided penalties for Banks.

Source: MDE FOIA response (September 25, 2026); MOECS public search (September 26, 2026).

Verify It Yourself

Anyone can reproduce this audit in minutes:

  1. Go to MOECS public search: mdoe.state.mi.us/MOECS/PublicCredentialSearch.aspx
  2. Enter the teacher’s last name
  3. Check: Is the certificate valid? Is it endorsed for the grades and subjects being taught?
  4. Compare results to the school’s actual staff roster at macdowellprep.com/about/

Discrepancies between MOECS endorsements and classroom assignments are visible immediately in the public record.

The Cost 📄 Documented

MacDowell Preparatory Academy serves 362 students. Four administrators draw $603,000/year in combined compensation:

MetricMacDowellContext
Admin cost per student$1,665/studentMichigan state average: approximately $850/student
Instructional spending32% of budgetMichigan target: 55–65%

Administration at nearly twice the state average per student diverts public funding away from instruction — in a school where MOECS already shows that most instructional staff lack proper credentials for their assignments.

This analysis is based entirely on MOECS public search results and Michigan Department of Education records. Every credential status can be independently verified using the steps above.

entry.title: Detroit Literacy Crisis — The Systemic View
entry.content:
MacDowell Preparatory Academy is not an anomaly — it is an extreme example of structural vulnerabilities in Michigan’s charter school oversight. This page connects the documented facts from this investigation to the broader patterns that enable them.

This analysis draws on the specific documented case to illustrate systemic patterns. The broader conclusions are the complainant’s analytical inference, supported by the specific evidence documented elsewhere on this site.

See also: Credential Audit, Funding Flow, Institutional Capture, Words vs. Numbers.

Five Structural Vulnerabilities

The MacDowell case documents five interlocking weaknesses in Michigan’s charter school accountability framework. The first four are structural mechanisms; the fifth is their cumulative effect on students.

1. Charter authorization as revenue 📄 Documented

Michigan authorizers receive 3% of state aid from each school they authorize. This creates a financial incentive to authorize and maintain schools regardless of performance.

At MacDowell Preparatory Academy, DPSCD (the authorizer) receives approximately $147K/year from that authorization fee alone — revenue that continues as long as the school remains open.

Source: MDE financial reports; charter authorization fee structure. See Funding Flow.

2. Management companies as extraction vehicles 📄 Documented

The Purpose Group LLC — Brian Banks’ management company — takes a 10% management fee plus all operating costs, totaling 72.67% of total revenue at MacDowell.

The fee-plus-cost-reimbursement structure means the management company can never lose money while the school absorbs all operational risk. Public per-pupil funding flows through the school entity; the majority exits to the LLC regardless of academic outcomes.

Source: MDE financial records; Purpose Group Management Agreement (FOIA). See Funding Flow and Purpose Group LLC.

3. Credential enforcement as theater 📄 Documented

The Michigan Department of Education investigated one name in four years at MacDowell — Brian Banks — in February 2022. The investigation was closed within approximately two hours after OEE Analyst Katie Schmiedeknecht communicated that “there will be no need for an investigation.”

MDE never checked the rest of the staff roster — despite MOECS and the Educator Registry being MDE’s own systems, searchable by any analyst in minutes. A MOECS audit on September 26, 2026 found that only 2 of 14 instructional staff are properly credentialed and correctly placed for their assignments.

Schmiedeknecht presents at state conferences on the same credential compliance rules her office is charged with enforcing — including slides stating that “Any teacher who is not appropriately placed may be subject to a salary deduction based on MCL 388.1763.” Her office failed to enforce those rules at MacDowell.

Source: MDE FOIA response (September 25, 2026); MOECS public search (September 26, 2026). See Credential Audit.

4. Board capture 📄 Documented

Judges, assistant attorneys general, and politicians sit on charter school boards, providing institutional legitimacy without corresponding accountability.

SchoolBoard ChairRole
MacDowell Preparatory AcademyJudge Tenisha Yancey36th District Court
Purpose Charter AcademyJudge Cylenthia MillerWayne County 3rd Circuit Court

These are not isolated appointments. The Institutional Capture analysis documents a broader pattern of judges, elected officials, and state employees serving on boards of schools connected to the Banks enterprise.

Source: School websites; Clutch Justice reporting (September 2026). See Tenisha Yancey, Cylenthia Miller.

5. Cumulative impact on students 📄 Documented

Every student at a bottom-3% school with 14% properly credentialed staff is a student who falls further behind. 362 students attend MacDowell Preparatory Academy.

MetricMacDowellSource
Math proficiency3%MDE, SchoolDigger
Statewide rankBottom 3% (1,443 of 1,488)SchoolDigger
Properly credentialed instructional staff2 of 14 (14%)MOECS audit, Sep 26, 2026
Enrollment362 studentsMDE records

The impact compounds annually. Students who enter kindergarten without credentialed teachers and leave middle school with 3% math proficiency carry deficits that accumulate across grade levels — not as a single-year failure, but as a structural outcome of the conditions documented above.

Source: MDE assessment data; SchoolDigger; Credential Audit.

The Numbers — General Context

The following points provide background context. They are cited as general patterns, not as specific statistics fabricated for this page.

  • Detroit’s overall literacy rates are among the lowest of any major American city.
  • Michigan has one of the highest proportions of charter school enrollment in the country.
  • Charter schools in Detroit have a wide performance range — some perform well, many do not.
  • The accountability mechanisms — authorizer oversight, MDE credential enforcement, financial auditing — have documented failure points at every level in this case. 📄 Documented

The specific numbers for MacDowell — 3% math proficiency, 72.67% revenue extraction, 14% properly credentialed staff — are documented on this site and in public records. The broader Detroit and Michigan context frames why a single school’s failure matters beyond its own walls.

What This Case Reveals 🔍 Inference

This is not just about Brian Banks. 🔍 Inference The structural vulnerabilities documented in this investigation exist across Michigan’s charter school sector:

  • Authorization incentives that prioritize revenue over oversight
  • Management company structures that extract more than they invest
  • Credential requirements that exist on paper but are not enforced
  • Governance structures that create conflicts of interest rather than accountability

Banks is the most extreme example documented in this investigation — 9 criminal convictions, fake credentials, 72.67% revenue extraction, 3% math proficiency. 📄 Documented But the structural enabling conditions are not unique to this case. 🔍 Inference

The same authorization fee model applies to every DPSCD-authorized charter. The same management company fee structure appears wherever a CMO operates under similar contract terms. The same MDE credential enforcement office serves every charter school in Michigan. The same board composition pattern — judges and public officials providing legitimacy — appears at multiple schools in this network.

MacDowell is the case study. The vulnerabilities are systemic. 🔍 Inference

Related Reporting

Independent journalism and public policy discussion provide broader context for the patterns documented here. This site does not reproduce those reports in full — it references them as external corroboration and context.

Clutch Justice

Clutch Justice has published reporting on Detroit charter school patterns connected to this investigation, including:

  • 📰 Clutch Justice : MacDowell: $15,217/student, 3% math proficiency — Academic and financial analysis of MacDowell’s extraction model, board composition, and DPSCD authorization chain
  • 📰 Clutch Justice : FOIA and Your Michigan School Board — Legal guide for parents requesting charter school records under Michigan FOIA

If exercised, the building would be owned by Purpose Group LLC — the same entity that employs all staff and takes 72.67% of revenue from the sister school, MacDowell Preparatory Academy.
